attributes.probed_form: P1: `static inline s32 towerBestCompletion(s32 best, u8* levelRecord, Player* p) { s32 value = *(s16*)(levelRecord + (s32)p + p->character * CHAR_SAVE_STRIDE + COMPLETION2_OFF); if (best > value) { return best; } best = value; return best; }` with the caller reduced to `levelRecord = (u8*)(requirement * 2); best = towerBestCompletion(best, levelRecord, p);` and the block-local `s32 value;` deleted. The aligned view shows ours `@0x128 ble ->130` / `@0x12c mr r0,r30` / `@0x130 mr r30,r0` against the target's `@0x124 ble ->12c` / `@0x128 b ->130` / `@0x12c mr r27,r0` -- the SAME inversion BF measured, so moving the load does not move the return web and BF's hypothesis is REFUTED. P2: the same helper made `static inline void towerBestCompletion(s32* best, u8* levelRecord, Player* p)` with `if (*best > value) { return; } *best = value;` and the caller `towerBestCompletion(&best, levelRecord, p);` -- the pair REFOLDED to the baseline's single `bgt`, i.e. taking the accumulator by pointer removes the inline's return value and with it the join the pair depends on.

hypothesis.statement: P1 and P2 bracket the answer: with a returned value the pair appears but the copy lands on the wrong path, and without one the pair vanishes. What has never been varied is WHICH of the two exits is the early return. Probe the mirror, `if (best <= value) { return value; } return best;` -- if the return web then coalesces with `value` (r0) the copy moves to the keep path and the emitted triple becomes the target's.
